title: Build the L2 explanation labeler and wire comments into feedback
description:
## Purpose

Build the L2 explanation labeler so arm A-c's analyst sees terse reviewer-style reasons, and wire comments into the harness feedback.

## Scope

- Labels stay the corpus reference labels for every arm; the LLM writes only the **reason**.
- One call per labeled item that some arm got wrong, conditioned on text + correct label, never on any arm's prediction (shared across arms). **≤300 calls**, about 100 expected. Model per Q1.
- Cache in `var/` keyed by item, label, prompt SHA-256 and model; exact replay. Text-free summaries: hashes, counts, a "mentions topic or domain" flag.
- Wire comments into `unified_loop._record_feedback` (`edit_comment_value`); record which promoted element cited which comment hashes. L0 = existing template; optional L3 (full rule) offline-only as a leakage ceiling, never evidence.
- Generate comments for the 300 labels.

## Definition of done

Specs first with a fake labeler, no network: cache replay is exact, summaries are text-free, comments reach the analyst briefing, attribution recorded. Comments generated and cached. Ends at the input to **S3**. Cost: ≤300 OpenAI calls (price unverified, expected cents); 0 Jev requests.

## Design

[DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md) §2 (labels with explanations, caveats), §6 step 7.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Q1 decided: build the labeler as a simulated human consulting its own hidden rubric (as in Jev-Flywheel's recorded simulated-labeler); real datasets later. The harness side is ready: --comments takes a JSONL of {item_id, comment} and arms A-c / A-c+F record them as edit_comment_value (a342823). Remaining: the labeler itself, its cache, and text-free summary flags.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Code done (Evaluations 49efdf3, 48d40de). unified_labeler.py: the simulated reviewer knows the corpus's planted convention (neutral sports talk -> positive, workplace operations -> negative; Jev-Flywheel README "The bias in the data") and writes a terse reason (<= 20 words, never states the rule; no comment for ~40% of labels, fixed by hash) conditioned only on text + reference label. Completion is pluggable: deterministic offline fake (Jev-Flywheel audit_corpus.py keyword cues), live gpt-6-luna via litellm with the gpt-6 shim (gated: --live --confirm, durable ledger, --max-calls <= 300 and >= the uncached need), or a refusing replay. Cache in var/ keyed by item, label, prompt SHA-256 and model, holding comments and hashes but no item text; reports are text-free (counts, comments hash, mentions-topic count). `unified_flywheel.py comments` writes the --comments JSONL. Steering records now carry comments_in_feedback and the hashes of comments the analyst's reply quoted; bundles record the same in rubric provenance. Specs: comments reach only A-c/A-c+F and appear in their analyst briefing (FlywheelHost.briefing), determinism, exact replay from cache, no dataset or comment text in outputs.

Surprise: Jev-Flywheel has no hidden-rubric labeler to reuse; its recorded simulated labeler uses the uninformative template only. The hidden rubric reused here is the corpus's own planted convention.

Offline twin: 300 labels -> 172 comments (128 skipped), 59 mention a topic. Remaining: the live generation (step 1 of the plan on the Phase 2 epic), then S3.
